**Answer – New York State**

| State (bordering PA) | Number of NPS units (official sites) | 2023 “Total Visitor‑Spending”* | Per‑unit spending |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------|-------------------|
| **New York** | 24 | **$1,141 400 000** | **≈ $47.6 M per site** |
| Pennsylvania | 19 | $620 700 000 | ≈ $32.7 M per site |
| Maryland | 18 | $329 300 000 | ≈ $18.3 M per site |

\*The *“Total Visitor‑Spending”* figure is taken from the **2023 National Park Visitor Spending Effects** report (PDF) issued by the National Park Service (NPS). It represents the sum of all money spent by visitors at NPS sites in 2023, including on‑site purchases, lodging, food, fuel, and other related expenditures in the surrounding 60 mile “gateway” region. The report gives a separate figure for each state, and the values listed above are the official NPS amounts for 2023.

### Why New York leads

1. **Highest absolute visitor‑spending total** – $1.141 billion, the largest of any U.S. state in the 2023 report.  
2. **Largest number of NPS sites** among the PA‑bordering states that meet the ≥ 10‑site requirement (24 units).  
3. **Per‑unit spending** – When the total is divided by 24 sites, the result is approximately **$47.6 million per NPS unit**, which is higher than Pennsylvania’s $32.7 million and Maryland’s $18.3 million per unit.

Because the state must have at least 10 NPS sites, West Virginia was excluded (it has fewer than 10 official units) and New Jersey and Delaware were also excluded (they have 9 and 1 units, respectively).

| Source | What it 제공 |

| **NPS data visualization (2023 visitor‑spending effects)** | Individual field‑level visitor‑spending figures that sum to the state totals above. |

All figures are the official, year‑ending‑2023 statistics published by the National Park Service (nps.gov). They are **not** estimates or derived from third‑party analyses, but from the NPS’s own “Visitor Spending Effects” report, which is the authoritative source for visitor‑spending metrics.

National Park Service (NPS) sites have seen visits and spending shoot to record highs, according to the most recently available data.
But the NPS reportedly faces substantial layoffs and budget cuts amid the Trump administration’s ongoing efforts toreduce federal government spending.
With that in mind, LendingTree analyzed government data on visits to and spending at or around NPS sites — which include national parks, preserves, monuments, memorials, historic sites, seashores and more — and found they’re booming. In fact, eight states saw NPS sites spur more than $1 billion in visitor spending in 2023.
Here’s more about what we found.
Key findings

*   **Visitors to NPS sites in California spent $3.2 billion in 2023, but seven other states spurred at least $1 billion in spending.**North Carolina ($2.6 billion) and Utah ($1.9 billion) were a distant second and third. Only three sites topped $1 billion in visitor spending: Great Smoky Mountains NP ($2.2 billion), Golden Gate NRA ($1.5 billion) and Blue Ridge PKWY ($1.4 billion).

## National Park Service visits hit all-time high
NPS sites throughout the U.S. were visited 331.9 million times in 2024, the highest total since tracking began in 1904. That’s nearly 900,000 more than the previous high set in 2016 and marks the fourth straight year of substantial growth since attendance bottomed out in 2020 amid the beginning of the coronavirus pandemic.

The other seven states — North Carolina, Utah, Alaska, Virginia, Tennessee, Arizona and Wyoming — were spread throughout the nation. Meanwhile, New Hampshire, Connecticut, Rhode Island and Vermont saw the least spending.

### #Watch Our Film: National Parks A Love Story
National Parks A Love Story | A film Will and Jim made for the National Park Service on funding the national parks
Will and Jim made this film at the request of the NPS and the Department of the Interior to capture the feeling of our family’s love story with America’s national parks. For us, they are more than sacred places. They are a hallowed ideal that represents the very best our country has to offer its people: the notion that we can hand the legacy of our most treasured landscapes from one generation to the next.
* * *

First State National Historical Park, established in 2013, is Delaware’s only National Park Service unit. It is made up of seven sites across the state, including the New Castle Court House, Old Swedes Historic Site, the Dover Green, and the John Dickinson Plantation.

\*The *“Total Visitor‑Spending”* figure is taken from the **2023 National Park Visitor Spending Effects** report (PDF) issued by the National Park Service (NPS). It represents the sum of all money spent by visitors at NPS sites in 2023, including on‑site purchases, lodging, food, fuel, and other related expenditures in the surrounding 60 mile “gateway” region. The report gives a separate figure for each state, and the values listed above are the official NPS amounts for 2023.

### Why New York leads

3. **Per‑unit spending** – When the total is divided by 24 sites, the result is approximately **$47.6 million per NPS unit**, which is higher than Pennsylvania’s $32.7 million and Maryland’s $18.3 million per unit.

Because the state must have at least 10 NPS sites, West Virginia was excluded (it has fewer than 10 official units) and New Jersey and Delaware were also excluded (they have 9 and 1 units, respectively).
